dedupe_keys.name: eea indicator diversion of waste from landfill in europe

description: This indicator from the European Environment Agency tracks how much waste European countries send to landfill and how that is changing, a key goal of EU waste policy under the waste hierarchy. The November 2025 edition reports that Europe's overall landfill rate fell from 23% to 17% between 2010 and 2022 while total waste generation kept rising; landfilled quantities in 2022 were 21% lower than in 2010, equal to 306 kg per EU citizen a year. Household and similar waste has been diverted well, but sorting residues sent to landfill doubled. The indicator presents amounts and shares landfilled by waste category for the EU-27 and by country, built on Eurostat waste statistics, with charts whose data can be downloaded. Coverage is the EU-27 and member countries from 2010 to 2022. The page and data are free to reuse with attribution under the EEA's standard reuse policy. Caveats: it relies on national reporting with differing definitions, figures lag several years, and the indicator shows landfill shares, not landfill capacity or sites. Simulation uses: setting landfill diversion trajectories in waste system scenarios and checking national progress against EU targets. Related records: Eurostat municipal waste statistics (data-eurostat-env-wasmun) give the underlying national figures and Eurostat waste shipments (data-eurostat-env-wasship-transboundary-waste-shipments) show exports of waste.
